visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 has a consistently correct projectile setup, trajectory, landing point, time, and final range despite a visually too-steep initial/component vector, whereas Lesson 1 repeatedly shows incorrect or garbled component values, confusing vector diagrams, nonsensical scales, and mislabeled quantities throughout.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 has a clearly wired, functional fill-in checkpoint after act_decomposition with a real prompt, accepted answers, hint, and remediation path, while Lesson 1 provides no gate specs or plan at all, so it has no functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2’s narration is clear, naturally paced, and uses spoken math appropriately, while Lesson 1 contains several garbled or unnatural phrases like “1 9.8 every second,” “0 verts,” and “X2” that would be read aloud as defects.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides timed visual cues that generally appear when the narration references the setup, trajectory, decomposition, vertical/horizontal focus, and formulas, whereas Lesson 1 has no beat or cue timing data at all, so it cannot demonstrate synchronized visual changes and is weaker on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 is more conceptually complete and pedagogically clear, explicitly stating assumptions, explaining component choice, using vertical motion to find time, and linking that time to horizontal range, while Lesson 1 is mostly correct but more terse, has awkward/possibly confusing phrasing, and gives less support for why the formulas apply.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has a much more visually composed, centered, and stylistically consistent presentation with large readable graphics, whereas Lesson 2 looks like an unpolished screen capture with persistent player controls, tiny/top-heavy text, large unused empty space, and raw backtick-style notation despite Lesson 1’s occasional garbled formula text.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner: five of six agents favored it, mostly with high confidence, including interactivity (0.98), narration quality (0.95), visual accuracy (0.88), sync (0.86), and concept accuracy (0.78). These dimensions indicate that Lesson 2 is more accurate, better synchronized, more pedagogically complete, and has functional learner interaction. Lesson 1 only won polish (0.72), due to a more composed visual style, but that single lower-confidence advantage is outweighed by Lesson 2’s strong performance across the core instructional and technical dimensions.
